context.description: The task-ui view state is one machine

evidence.trustReason: The real plugin key test asserts visible design, selection, expansion, watch and stop results, but never observes the plugin-created actor snapshot. The snapshot and 5-second disarm assertions drive a separate actor with synthetic events, so they do not prove those plugin keys use one machine. Counting createActor/createSignal text and checking a constructor line do not establish that all plugin handlers and readers use that actor rather than parallel state. The 1 s, 2 s, 1.5 s and 500 ms cadence assertions also attach liveSessions and liveTail to the separate actor, not the installed plugin readers. Invalid status retention is asserted in both paths, but the one-machine and plugin-cadence claims lack direct linkage.

context.gherkin:
Scenario: UI2 The task-ui view state is one machine
    Given the task-ui plugin started for a session
    When the user switches design, selects a task, expands, watches and presses the stop key once
    Then the design, the selection, the expansion, the watch target and the stop-key arming are states and context of one view machine
    And the stop key disarms 5 seconds after it was armed
    And the status, session list, activity lines and proof-log tail are read by delayed transitions every 1 s, 2 s, 1.5 s and 500 ms
    And a status text that does not parse keeps the last good status

  @phase4 @permissions @ops
